answer: Recursive zero‑knowledge reputation commitments bind an agent’s history to a succinct proof, so forging a clone requires solving an NP‑hard discrete‑log puzzle. A verifiable delay primitive stretches the commitment over a fixed window, making any identity duplication cost exponential time and negligible success probability. The consensus beacon re‑validates each transition; copper hard computational cost, combined with the nectar of trust, renders Sybil attacks economically prohibitive under one‑third Byzantine tolerance.
